svg.title: Sodium disorders decision chart: hypernatremia sorted by ECF volume, urine volume and urine osmolality into non-renal water loss, diabetes insipidus (central or nephrogenic by desmopressin) or renal solute loss; hyponatremia sorted by plasma osmolality, urine osmolality, urine sodium and ECF volume into water excess, low effective volume, endocrine causes including SIADH, or renal salt loss; with the rules for how fast to correct each

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif
Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif
Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif
Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: Sodium is off: is water LOST (Na > 144) or RETAINED (Na < 136)?

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: both are almost always WATER problems, not sodium problems

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: find the CAUSE, and correct only as fast as the brain can adapt (CORRECT row)

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: HYPERnatremia (Na > 144): free water LOST · cells SHRINK

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: unusual unless THIRST, ACCESS to water or ability to DRINK fails

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: 1 · extracellular fluid (ECF) volume HIGH → sodium GAIN: sea water, IV fluids, mineralocorticoid excess

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif
Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: 1 · plasma osmolality (Osm) HIGH or normal → PSEUDOhyponatremia: glucose, mannitol (Na falls 1 per 3–4 rise in glucose)

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: 2 · ECF volume LOW: how much URINE, and how concentrated?

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: 2 · Plasma Osm LOW (TRUE): URINE Osm, then URINE Na, then ECF

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: urine Osm > 100 = ADH is ON · urine Na < 20 = the kidney senses low volume
